title: Conjecture 1.4 (Ordered Binary Matrix Removal Lemma)
statement_text: For any finite family $\mathcal{F}$ of ordered binary matrices and any $\varepsilon > 0$ there exists $\delta = \delta(\mathcal{F}, \varepsilon)$ such that any $n \times n$ binary matrix which is $\varepsilon$-far from $\mathcal{F}$-freeness contains at least $\delta n^{a+b}$ copies of some $a \times b$ matrix from $\mathcal{F}$.
context_text: Alon, Fischer and Newman obtained an efficient conditional regularity lemma for ordered binary matrices and conjectured that it could be used to yield a removal lemma for ordered binary matrices. This paper proves Theorem 1.8, an infinite ordered matrix removal lemma that settles a generalized form of this conjecture, extending it to finite or infinite families over any finite alphabet.
paper_contribution: Proves Theorem 1.8 (Infinite Ordered Matrix Removal Lemma), which settles a generalized form of this conjecture for any finite or infinite family of ordered matrices over any finite alphabet $\Sigma$.
paper_title: Testing hereditary properties of ordered graphs and matrices

title: Open Problem: Regularity-free proof for the ordered removal lemma
statement_text: It will be interesting to try to obtain a proof for the ordered graph removal lemma that does not go through the strong regularity lemma needed in the current proof.
context_text: An ordered graph over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ ($|\Sigma|\ge2$) is an edge-coloured complete graph $G:\binom{[n]}{2}\to\Sigma$ on a totally ordered vertex set (ordinary graphs correspond to $\Sigma=\{0,1\}$); the ordered (induced) subgraph on $u_1<\dots<u_k$ is $H(ij)=G(u_iu_j)$, and $G$ is $\mathcal{F}$-free if none of its ordered subgraphs lies in $\mathcal{F}$. $G$ is $\epsilon$-far from $\mathcal{F}$-freeness if one must change at least $\epsilon\binom{n}{2}$ edge values to make it $\mathcal{F}$-free. The authors' ordered removal lemma states: for every (finite or infinite) family $\mathcal{F}$ of ordered graphs and every $\epsilon>0$ there are $q_0$ and $\delta>0$ such that every ordered graph $G$ on $n$ vertices that is $\epsilon$-far from $\mathcal{F}$-freeness contains at least $\delta n^q$ induced ordered copies of some $F\in\mathcal{F}$ on $q\le q_0$ vertices; consequently every hereditary property of ordered graphs is strongly testable (testable with a number of queries independent of $n$). An analogous lemma holds for ordered matrices $M:[m]\times[n]\to\Sigma$, with copies being submatrices on increasing rows and columns. The proof relies on strong variants of the regularity lemma: Szemerédi's regularity lemma already imposes a tower-type dependence of $\delta^{-1}$ on $\epsilon^{-1}$, and the variant used is at least as strong as the strong regularity lemma of Alon, Fischer, Krivelevich and Szegedy, which has a wowzer-type (tower of towers) dependence; for infinite families the dependence may be arbitrarily bad. Fox gave the first proof of the (unordered) graph removal lemma that avoids the regularity lemma, though still with tower-type dependence. The open problem is to find a proof of the ordered removal lemma that does not go through strong regularity.
notes: Stated as a research direction in Section 1.3 without a formal labelled environment.

title: Open Problem: Better parameter dependence for ordered binary matrix removal
statement_text: It will be interesting to combine the ideas from the current proof with the binary matrix regularity lemma of Alon, Fischer and Newman to obtain a removal lemma for finite families of ordered binary matrices with better dependence between the parameters $\delta^{-1}$ and $\varepsilon^{-1}$; ideally polynomial dependence, but even exponential dependence would be interesting.
context_text: An ordered graph over a finite alphabet $\Sigma$ ($|\Sigma|\ge2$) is an edge-coloured complete graph $G:\binom{[n]}{2}\to\Sigma$ on a totally ordered vertex set (ordinary graphs correspond to $\Sigma=\{0,1\}$); the ordered (induced) subgraph on $u_1<\dots<u_k$ is $H(ij)=G(u_iu_j)$, and $G$ is $\mathcal{F}$-free if none of its ordered subgraphs lies in $\mathcal{F}$. $G$ is $\epsilon$-far from $\mathcal{F}$-freeness if one must change at least $\epsilon\binom{n}{2}$ edge values to make it $\mathcal{F}$-free. The authors' ordered removal lemma states: for every (finite or infinite) family $\mathcal{F}$ of ordered graphs and every $\epsilon>0$ there are $q_0$ and $\delta>0$ such that every ordered graph $G$ on $n$ vertices that is $\epsilon$-far from $\mathcal{F}$-freeness contains at least $\delta n^q$ induced ordered copies of some $F\in\mathcal{F}$ on $q\le q_0$ vertices; consequently every hereditary property of ordered graphs is strongly testable (testable with a number of queries independent of $n$). An analogous lemma holds for ordered matrices $M:[m]\times[n]\to\Sigma$, with copies being submatrices on increasing rows and columns. For binary matrices, $\Sigma=\{0,1\}$. Alon, Fischer and Newman obtained an efficient conditional regularity lemma for ordered binary matrices, in which $\delta^{-1}$ is polynomial in $\epsilon^{-1}$, and conjectured that it could yield a removal lemma for finite families of ordered binary matrices; the present paper proves such a removal lemma (in a generalized form, for any finite alphabet and infinite families), but its proof uses a variant of the strong regularity lemma and so inherits a wowzer-type (tower of towers) dependence of $\delta^{-1}$ on $\epsilon^{-1}$. The problem is to obtain, for finite families of ordered binary matrices, a removal lemma with polynomial, or even exponential, dependence of $\delta^{-1}$ on $\epsilon^{-1}$. More generally, the authors ask for large families of hereditary ordered graph or matrix properties with more efficient testers.
